name: MCP9808T-E_MS
title: ±0.5 °C maximum accuracy digital temperature sensor with I2C/SMBus interface
summary: The MCP9808 measures its own die temperature with a band-gap sensor and a delta-sigma converter and reports it over a 400 kHz two-wire bus that works with I2C and SMBus hosts. Accuracy is ±0.5 °C at most from -20 °C to +100 °C and ±1 °C at most from -40 °C to +125 °C, with resolution selectable from 0.5 °C down to 0.0625 °C. An open-drain Alert pin compares the reading with programmable upper, lower and critical limits and can act as a thermostat output or a host interrupt. It runs from 2.7 V to 5.5 V, draws 200 µA typical and 0.1 µA typical in shutdown, and comes in an 8-lead 2x3 mm DFN and an 8-lead MSOP.
key_figures: 8 per address code (A2, A1, A0); a second code doubles that to 16

SHDN cannot be set to 1 while either lock bit is 1, but it can be cleared to 0 while locked.
In shutdown all power-hungry circuits stop, yet every register stays readable and writable.
Once set, Crit. Lock stays 1 until an internal reset, and Win. Lock until a power-on reset.
THYST, both lock bits, Alert Cnt., Alert Sel., Alert Pol. and Alert Mod. can be written in shutdown; the Alert output neither asserts nor releases then.
Int. Clear cannot be set to 1 in shutdown, though it can be cleared after the part has entered shutdown.
Alert Stat. cannot be changed in shutdown, except that clearing an interrupt with bit 5 in shutdown also clears it.

circuits.title: Active-low Alert output configuration
circuits.description: The Alert pin is an open-drain transistor to ground inside the part, so a pull-up resistor RPU from VDD to the pin gives the Alert output its high level. With the active-low setting the output sits high and the part pulls it low on an alert.

operation.text: A band-gap temperature sensor produces a voltage proportional to absolute temperature, which a delta-sigma ADC turns into a digital word. The result, the limits, the configuration and the identification codes sit in user registers reached through a two-wire interface compatible with SMBus and I2C.

The part is a slave on a Standard-mode compatible two-wire bus running up to 400 kHz. A transfer opens with a start condition, then the 7-bit address and the R/W bit, and the receiver acknowledges every byte; a stop ends it, and a new transfer may begin after tB-FREE. A start or stop arriving mid-transfer makes the part let go of the bus. When reading, the host answers the last byte with a NAK so the part frees SDA for the stop. Data on SDA must be settled before SCL rises and changes only while SCL is low.

Registers cannot be read or written in sequence: each one is chosen by writing the register pointer first. The part keeps the last pointer, so later reads of the same register can begin straight with a start and the address byte. The pointer is an 8-bit write-only register whose low four bits select the register; its upper four bits must be 0.
The address is 0011 followed by the levels on A2, A1 and A0, giving eight parts on one bus. A second code, 1001 plus the pins, is available from the factory, so up to sixteen parts can share a bus.
If SCL stays low or high for tOUT (25 ms to 35 ms) the part resets its serial interface, which sets the slowest clock the bus can use. The part never stretches the clock.

TA is a 16-bit read-only register holding 13 bits of two's complement temperature: a sign and twelve bits from 2^7 °C to 2^-4 °C. Its temperature bits are double-buffered, so the host can read while the next conversion runs, and a fresh result is loaded every tCONV. The top three bits flag TA ≥ TCRIT, TA > TUPPER and TA < TLOWER, so the cause of an alert can be read back. Data above +32 °C sits in the upper byte; the lower byte holds the rest down to the fractional bits.
The Resolution register at 0000 1000b sets 0.5, 0.25, 0.125 or 0.0625 °C per bit, with typical conversion times of 30, 65, 130 and 250 ms. The factory default after power-on is 0.0625 °C.

TUPPER and TLOWER set a temperature window and TCRIT a critical limit. Each is a 16-bit read/write register holding 11 bits of two's complement data in 0.25 °C steps. With the Alert output enabled, leaving the window or passing TCRIT asserts Alert.

Setting CONFIG bit 8 stops conversions and every power-consuming circuit while the serial interface stays alive; the part then draws ISHDN and TA keeps the last reading. Clearing the bit or cycling power restarts continuous conversion. Bus traffic raises the shutdown current, and so does an Alert output left asserted, since the part holds that state through shutdown.

CONFIG bits 10 and 9 add 0, +1.5, +3 or +6 °C of hysteresis to TUPPER, TLOWER and TCRIT to stop the output chattering. It acts only on falling temperature: a limit is released once the temperature drops below the limit minus THYST.

CONFIG bit 3 enables Alert, bit 0 picks comparator or interrupt behaviour and bit 1 picks active-high or active-low. The pin is open drain and needs a pull-up. CONFIG bit 4 reports whether Alert is asserted. Bit 2 turns Alert into a critical-temperature output alone, which behaves as a comparator and ignores bit 0. Whenever the temperature rises past TCRIT, Alert becomes a comparator output whatever bit 0 says, and goes back to the selected mode once the temperature falls below TCRIT minus THYST.

Alert is asserted while the temperature is outside the limits and released when it comes back inside them, with hysteresis on the way down. Entering shutdown with Alert asserted leaves it asserted; the part must convert again for tCONV with the limit conditions met before Alert releases. This mode suits thermostat jobs such as running a fan or shutting a system down above a safe temperature.

Alert is asserted each time TA crosses TUPPER or TLOWER and stays asserted until the host writes 1 to CONFIG bit 5. Shutdown does not clear it. This mode cannot be used together with the critical-only setting of bit 2. It is meant for interrupt-driven microcontroller systems.
CONFIG bit 7 locks TCRIT and bit 6 locks TUPPER and TLOWER against being overwritten by mistake, which would cause false alerts. Once set they hold until power is removed and reapplied.
An internal power-on reset returns every register to its default whenever VDD dips below VPOR (2.2 V typical on a falling supply).
The Manufacturer ID register reads 0x0054. The Device ID and Revision register reads 0x04 in its upper byte and the silicon revision in its lower byte, 0x00 for the first release.

Nothing but the host is needed to measure temperature. A high-frequency ceramic capacitor of 0.1 µF to 1 µF between VDD and GND, as near the pins as possible, is advised against noise. Because the die reads the board's temperature through its pins, a ground layer under the pins improves thermal coupling; the DFN layout puts the exposed pad, pin 9, in the middle under the part.

With the low supply current, self-heating is normally negligible. Heavy pull-up loads on SDA, SCL and Alert raise it: sinking the maximum specified current on the bus pins can add an error of about +0.5 °C.
